messages:
ellen_northwind: Hey team — our prod app (Northwind) just started returning wrong tool outputs for some requests. Two tools called in parallel (geo_lookup, price_lookup) but the results look swapped in the response. High traffic right now, customer-facing page shows wrong prices. request id: nw-req-9923 x-correlation-id: nw-req-9923

maria_support: sorry to hear that — can you paste the raw request payload + the response you got? Also which SDK version and region?

ellen_northwind: payload below (redacted keys). SDK node v2.8.1, region us-east-1. Response has price_lookup results under "geo_lookup" key and vice versa.
```json
{
  "request_id": "nw-req-9923",
  "model": "rwd/llama-3-8b",
  "tools": [
    {"name": "geo_lookup", "args": {"ip": "54.23.12.11"}},
    {"name": "price_lookup", "args": {"sku": "NW-199"}}
  ],
  "parallel": true
}
```
response (redacted):
```json
{
  "tool_results": [
    {"name": "geo_lookup", "output": "$19.99"},
    {"name": "price_lookup", "output": "Seattle, WA"}
  ]
}
```

maria_support: yikes. tagging infra + ml. david, any immediate logs for nw-req-9923? Sam, can we check if this triggered any billing anomalies?

opsbot: New escalation created: ESCL-8732 (priority: P1) — assigned to #support oncall.

maria_support: quick question — are you using the SDK multi-tool fanout helper (multi_tool_use) or making parallel calls in app code?

ellen_northwind: we're calling the SDK helper exactly like docs example: multiToolCall([...]) — we don't fanout ourselves.

maria_support: thanks — can you try toggling parallel -> false as a quick mitigation? We can test repro too.

ellen_northwind: toggled to parallel false and the issue disappeared. But we need parallel for latency.

maria_support: copying the raw server-side logs we got for nw-req-9923 from the customer-provided header trace (redacted ids):
```
2026-02-14T15:21:10.124Z INFO  inbound req nw-req-9923 started route /v1/generate
2026-02-14T15:21:10.125Z DEBUG dispatching 2 tool calls (fanout id=fan-7a3c)
2026-02-14T15:21:10.126Z DEBUG tool_call queued geo_lookup call_id=lc-1001
2026-02-14T15:21:10.126Z DEBUG tool_call queued price_lookup call_id=lc-1002
2026-02-14T15:21:10.201Z DEBUG tool_response received call_id=lc-1002 -> attached to fanout idx=0
2026-02-14T15:21:10.202Z DEBUG tool_response received call_id=lc-1001 -> attached to fanout idx=1
2026-02-14T15:21:10.203Z ERROR association failed: expected mapping for call_id lc-1001 -> idx=0 but got idx=1
```

maria_support: looks like tool_response handler associated by arrival index rather than call_id. david?

david_infra: digging. initial hypothesis: race in the fanout assembly where we were using an incremental array push keyed by arrival order, and a race caused wrong slot assignment when two responses arrived very close together. I can repro locally with a stress harness.

david_infra: repro harness (simplified):
```js
// pseudo
const calls = [geo, price];
const results = [];
await Promise.all(calls.map(async (c, i) => {
  const res = await invokeTool(c);
  // previous logic: results.push(res); // order not preserved on concurrent pushes
  results[i] = res; // suggested fix
}));
```
jenn_ml: thanks. quick clarification — do tool_result objects include any per-call unique id right now? If we had a tool_call_id propagated back in the tool_result we could use that instead of relying on ordering.

david_infra: right now tool responses carry call_id in transport headers but the fanout assembly code was matching by position only in the consumer path. transport header example: `X-Tool-Call-ID: lc-1002`. But the assembly layer didn't read it.

jenn_ml: that explains it. two suggested fixes: 1) urgent hotfix: match responses by tool_call_id header when present, fall back to index. 2) longer term: ensure SDK assigns stable uuid per tool call and we propagate tool_call_id through the whole pipeline and into billing records.

sam_sre: billing note: when results are associated to wrong tool names we can misattribute egress/compute units. we saw a single customer invoice spike of +0.8% last hour matching these requests. need a reconciliation run for ESCL-8732.

maria_support: action items: david to put hotfix (match by header) behind a feature flag (ff.fanout_callid_assoc) and roll to canary; jenn to coordinate SDK change to emit tool_call_id; sam to run billing reconciliation; ellen, we'll keep parallel enabled in canary only for you after we validate.

david_infra: creating PR now. patch summary:
- fanout assembler: if X-Tool-Call-ID header present, use stable map call_id -> slot index; otherwise preserve original index assignment.
- add extra logging: WARN when arrival order != expected and no call_id present.

maria_support: can you attach the repro script for infra so eng-repro can run against staging? ellen provided a short curl earlier, we added a small harness: 
```bash
# repro.sh (uses curl + two mocked tool endpoints)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Correlation-Id: nw-req-9923" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd/llama-3-8b","tools":[{"name":"geo_lookup","args":{"ip":"54.23.12.11"}},{"name":"price_lookup","args":{"sku":"NW-199"}}],"parallel":true}'
```

ellen_northwind: thanks — approved canary. please keep me posted, this hits checkout path for many sessions.

opsbot: Rollout plan: will deploy ff.fanout_callid_assoc=true to 5% canary, monitor association WAL logs and customer metric "tool_assoc_mismatch_rate" for 30m.

jenn_ml: follow-up: we'll also add schema guidance to tool_result to include `tool_call_id` string and `tool_name` fields to avoid ambiguity in future. SDKs should round-trip these.

maria_support: noted. logging ticket ESCL-8732 updated with PR link, canary URL and customer contact. I'll handle comms to the customer.

ellen_northwind: appreciate the quick response. I'll monitor canary and report any anomalies.

sam_sre: running billing reconciliation job now, will post delta once complete.

maria_support: thanks everyone — keeping thread open until mismatch rate is zero for nw-req-9923 class and we have SDK patch tracked.

{"note": "end of thread"}
